label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 5 evaluation (recorded window, frozen bundle)

attempts.validity: all complete True, pending max 4.0, failures 0, server errors 0.0, pool timeouts 0, other edges 0

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low

report.summary: During the window, outbox publication kept pace with arrivals and deliveries were fast. No backlog, failures, pool pressure or DB blocking were seen, so late notifications are not reproduced here.

findings.claim: Outbox kept up: 450 arrivals and 450 publications, no backlog. Pending stayed at 1-4 and oldest undelivered age was at most 1.23 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals minus publications was 0 and the outbox was settled; pending and age stayed flat.

findings.claim: All 450 deliveries succeeded on attempt 1 in about 71 ms, mostly consumer auth time. There were no retries or errors.
findings.reason: Outcome counts show 450 successes and 0 failures; the p95 total was 75.6 ms.

findings.claim: No upstream contention: transfers had 0 server errors and p99 0.248 s. The pool had 0 timeouts and no pending borrowers, and no DB blocking was sampled.
findings.reason: Request, pool and blocker metrics were all clean with complete coverage.

limitations: The window is only 150 s, and the consumer is a test fixture, so real customer notification delivery was not observed.
Pending, pool and blocker data are sampled gauges and can miss brief spikes.
next_checks: Re-run the checks over the time when customers reported delays, including any later notification-channel stage.
Compare event creation time with customer-visible notification time end to end.

alternatives.reason: Only the HTTP delivery to the fixture consumer was measured; later stages are not visible.
alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurs outside this window or in a downstream notification channel beyond the consumer endpoint.

alternatives.reason: Acquire max was 5 ms and oldest undelivered age never exceeded 1.23 s, though gauges are sampled.
alternatives.hypothesis: Brief sub-scrape or sub-2s stalls (pool saturation, DB blocks) caused delays.

report.summary: Outbox, delivery, pool, DB and request sources all show healthy behavior in the window; no cause of late notifications was observed.

findings.claim: Outbox publishes at the arrival rate with no backlog: 450 arrivals, 450 publications, 0 failed, pending 1-4, oldest undelivered age at most 1.23 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals minus publications is 0 and the outbox is settled, with a small stable pending gauge.

findings.claim: Deliveries are fast and clean: all 450 attempts succeeded on attempt 1 with status 200, p95 about 76 ms, mostly consumer auth time.
findings.reason: No errors or retries, and latency is far below the 3000 ms delivery timeout.

findings.claim: No upstream contention: pool had 0 timeouts and no pending borrowers, no DB blocking was sampled, and transfers had 0 server errors with p99 0.248 s.
findings.reason: Request, pool and blocker sources are all clean over the window.

limitations: The window is only 150 s and may not include the period when customers saw delays.
Pending, pool and blocker data are sampled gauges and can miss brief events; consumer is a test fixture.
next_checks: Re-run over the time of the actual customer complaints, comparing notification send times to commit times.
Inspect the downstream notification pipeline after the consumer endpoint.

alternatives.reason: Timings only cover up to the consumer's HTTP response; later notification stages are not observed.
alternatives.hypothesis: Delay occurs downstream of LedgerCore (consumer or notification provider after the 200 response).

alternatives.reason: Durable counts and max oldest-undelivered age of 1.23 s show no stall, though gauges are sampled.
alternatives.hypothesis: Brief outbox poll or pool stalls shorter than the sampling intervals.
